continuity_scope: Medieval Icelandic textual witnesses only; Poetic Edda and Prose Edda remain distinguished, with selected heroic poems included as Poetic Edda witnesses.
continuity: Medieval Icelandic textual witnesses; no harmonized pan-Norse continuity
work_or_witness: Poetic Edda (as translated by Henry Adams Bellows, 1936)
edition: Public-domain English translation of the Codex Regius poems, Project Gutenberg eBook 14726
scope: Named agents in the selected mythological and heroic poems, with prose evidence used only where stated; names and attributes are not silently transferred between witnesses.
coverage_rule: A representative foundational pass of major named divine, jötunn, monstrous, supernatural, and heroic agents who materially act in the selected Eddic witnesses or exemplify a distinct named ontological/narrative category. It is not a census of every name, epithet, regional tradition, archaeological source, later saga, or modern reconstruction.
omissions: Most minor named beings in þulur/catalogues and incidental kennings.
Regional and post-medieval Scandinavian folklore, archaeological iconography, skaldic corpus, and later saga traditions unless a specific witness is added in a later pass.
Characters whose only inclusion rationale would be a generic ontology category rather than material action or a distinctive represented category.
uncertainties: The dating, composition, and relationship of individual poems and Snorri's prose retellings are scholarly questions; this pass indexes witnesses, not a recovered pre-Christian canon.
Æsir/Vanir and jötunn are source terms with shifting genealogical and narrative use; they are not treated as fixed fantasy races.
Some figures occur under variant spellings or are distinguished differently in prose and verse; aliases preserve discoverability while records retain the named witness basis.
completion_status: pass-complete for the declared Eddic witness scope only
evidence_basis: Primary-text citations to the Bellows Poetic Edda and Brodeur Prose Edda translations, with poem/stanza or book/chapter locators; no Wikipedia, fan-wiki, or adaptation evidence used.
